subtopic: Nomenclature and Structure of Carboxyl Group
stem:
Give the IUPAC names of the following compounds:
(i) \(\text{Ph CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}\)
(ii) \((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CHCOOH}\)
(iii) A cyclopentane ring bearing a \(\text{-COOH}\) group on one carbon and a \(\text{-CH}_3\) group on the adjacent carbon
(iv) A benzene ring bearing a \(\text{-COOH}\) group, with \(\text{-NO}_2\) groups on both carbons ortho to it and a third \(\text{-NO}_2\) group on the carbon para to it
_note: The book prints (iii) and (iv) as structural drawings. Both were read at 3x-4x zoom: (iii) is a cyclopentane with CH3 and COOH on adjacent ring carbons; (iv) is a benzene ring carrying COOH with NO2 at both ortho positions and one at the para position. Described in words rather than reproduced as a figure since the substitution pattern is the whole content of the question.

subtopic: Methods of Preparation of Carboxylic Acids
stem:
Write chemical reactions to affect the following transformations:
(i) Butan-1-ol to butanoic acid
(ii) Benzyl alcohol to phenylethanoic acid
(iii) 3-Nitrobromobenzene to 3-nitrobenzoic acid
(iv) 4-Methylacetophenone to benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid
(v) Cyclohexene to hexane-1,6-dioic acid
(vi) Butanal to butanoic acid.
solution:
(i) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow[\text{Jones reagent}]{\text{CrO}_3\text{-H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}\) (butan-1-ol to butanoic acid)

(ii) \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{HBr}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \xrightarrow{\text{KCN}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{CN} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{H}_3\text{O}^{+}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}\) (phenylethanoic acid)

(iii) 3-Nitrobromobenzene \(\xrightarrow[\text{ether}]{\text{Mg}}\) 3-nitrophenylmagnesium bromide \(\xrightarrow{\text{CO}_2\ (\text{dry ice})}\) the carboxylate \(\text{-COOMgBr}\) \(\xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^{+}}\) 3-nitrobenzoic acid

(iv) 4-Methylacetophenone \(\xrightarrow{\text{KMnO}_4/\text{KOH}}\) dipotassium benzene-1,4-dicarboxylate \(\xrightarrow{\text{dil. H}_2\text{SO}_4}\) benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid (terephthalic acid)

(v) Cyclohexene \(\xrightarrow[\text{Heat}]{\text{KMnO}_4\text{-H}_2\text{SO}_4}\) \(\text{HOOC}(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{COOH}\), hexane-1,6-dioic acid (adipic acid)

(vi) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} \xrightarrow[\text{(Tollens' reagent)}]{\text{Ammoniacal AgNO}_3} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}\) (butanoic acid)
_note: The book prints this solution as six drawn reaction schemes on the following page (p-21); transcribed here as equations. In (iii) the Grignard route is drawn on the ring.

subtopic: Methods of Preparation of Carboxylic Acids
stem:
Show how each of the following compounds can be converted to benzoic acid.
(i) Ethylbenzene
(ii) Acetophenone
(iii) Bromobenzene
(iv) Phenylethene (Styrene)

Which acid of each pair shown here would you expect to be stronger?
(i) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}\) or \(\text{CH}_2\text{FCO}_2\text{H}\)
(ii) \(\text{CH}_2\text{FCO}_2\text{H}\) or \(\text{CH}_2\text{ClCO}_2\text{H}\)
(iii) \(\text{CH}_2\text{FCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}\) or \(\text{CH}_3\text{CHFCH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}\)
(iv) \(p\)-Trifluoromethylbenzoic acid, \(\text{F}_3\text{C-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{-COOH}\), or \(p\)-methylbenzoic acid, \(\text{H}_3\text{C-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{-COOH}\)
_note: In (iv) the book draws two para-disubstituted benzene rings; transcribed as formulae with the para relationship stated.
